payload.title: Cytokine exposure alters HepG2 acute phase protein secretion
payload.abstract: Inflammatory signalling modulates hepatic protein synthesis and may confound toxicological readouts. HepG2 cells were treated with interleukin-6 and tumour necrosis factor alpha at physiological concentrations for 24 hours. C-reactive protein secretion increased more than twenty-fold and albumin secretion fell by roughly half. Viability was unaffected across the range examined. The agents used here are recombinant proteins rather than small-molecule drugs, and the study reports a secretory phenotype rather than a pharmacological potency value for any compound. Transcriptomic profiling confirmed induction of the canonical acute phase programme, and the magnitude of the albumin decrease tracked the interleukin-6 concentration across the range examined.
